messages.content:
You are a senior hedge-fund analyst filing statements into a library of open questions about NVIDIA and its world. For each statement, return the ids of the questions it is filed under, or an empty list. Read each question's 'takes' line: it says what that question collects. A statement filed under no question is a valid answer, not a failure: never file a statement under a question it does not bear on because no better question exists.
File each statement under the narrowest question that names its matter, and under that one only; never add a broader question beside it. A company-wide figure question (total revenue, segment revenue, gross margin, operating margin, profit, capex) takes only the company's own reported figures, guidance, estimates of that figure and management's statements about it. News about a customer, supplier, competitor, product, policy or deal is filed under the question that names that matter (an event, a policy process, a theme), or under none when no question names it. A rumour is filed exactly as a confirmed statement is.

[Item] tomshardware.com, 2026-07-02: Nvidia offers to take a cut of AI cloud revenue on top of hardware sales in new optional financing vehicle — trades tokens for revenue cut

[Open questions]
  - v1 (NVDA, due 2027-02-28): How much will NVIDIA’s disclosed commitments for guarantees and similar obligations to cloud providers reach in its FY2027 annual filing?
      takes: financing_amount figures, guidance, estimates and revisions for NVIDIA commitments and guarantees to cloud providers over 2026-02-01..2027-01-31, and the direct drivers of that figure stated with a size; statements about the matter 'NVIDIA cloud-provider financing and capacity partnerships' (also called AI Compute Partnership, DSX AI Factory, AI Compute Partnership Program, Firmus, Sharon AI, Lambda): NVIDIA’s financial guarantees, capacity-purchase commitments, leasebacks, and revenue-sharing arrangements with cloud providers and data-center customers. belong here under any of those names
  - v2 (NVDA, due 2027-12-31): Will NVIDIA sign or announce a financial guarantee for OpenAI’s Ohio data-center lease by 2027-12-31?
      takes: the terms, amounts, counterparties, agreements and approvals of this obligation or deal, and its steps, confirmations and denials: OpenAI Ohio data-center lease guarantee; statements about the matter 'NVIDIA cloud-provider financing and capacity partnerships' (also called AI Compute Partnership, DSX AI Factory, AI Compute Partnership Program, Firmus, Sharon AI, Lambda): NVIDIA’s financial guarantees, capacity-purchase commitments, leasebacks, and revenue-sharing arrangements with cloud providers and data-center customers. belong here under any of those names
  - v3 (NVDA, due 2027-02-24): How much financing and other commitment exposure will Nvidia report for its AI-cloud customer backstop arrangements at the FY2027 annual filing?
      takes: financing_amount figures, guidance, estimates and revisions for AI-cloud customer backstop arrangements over 2026-02-01..2027-01-31, and the direct drivers of that figure stated with a size; statements about the matter 'NVIDIA cloud-provider financing and capacity partnerships' (also called AI Compute Partnership, DSX AI Factory, AI Compute Partnership Program, Firmus, Sharon AI, Lambda): NVIDIA’s financial guarantees, capacity-purchase commitments, leasebacks, and revenue-sharing arrangements with cloud providers and data-center customers. belong here under any of those names

[Statements]
  - e1 [fact] who: Nvidia | Nvidia announced a business model combining its hardware sales to partner AI clouds with an ongoing percentage of revenue generated by that hardware; no percentage was disclosed. | quote: Nvidia has announced a new business model under which it’ll be able to double-dip for revenue on the same silicon: once when its partner AI clouds use its hardware, and again as an ongoing percentage of the revenue that hardware generates.
  - e2 [party_statement] who: Nvidia and CFO Colette Kress | Nvidia CFO Colette Kress and the company described the model as a way to provide compute access to startups unable to finance it themselves. | quote: In a blog post co-authored by CFO Colette Kress, the company pitched the “revenue-sharing and credit-support model” as a way to open compute access to startups that can’t finance it themselves.
  - e3 [third_party_view] who: Tom's Hardware | Nvidia named Australia's Sharon AI and Singapore-based Firmus Technologies as the first partners in the model. | quote: Australia's Sharon AI and Singapore-based Firmus Technologies are the first named partners.
  - e4 [party_statement] who: Nvidia | Nvidia said the participating clouds would buy its infrastructure and sell cloud services, while Nvidia would receive hardware revenue plus a percentage of cloud income earned on the capacity. | quote: Under the structure, participating AI clouds procure Nvidia infrastructure and sell Nvidia-powered cloud services to end customers. Nvidia collects its usual product revenue on the hardware plus a percentage of the cloud income earned on th
  - e5 [rumour] who: Bloomberg | Bloomberg reported that developers receive token credits in exchange for a share of future sales; Nvidia and its partners had not disclosed the revenue-split percentages. | quote: Per Bloomberg , developers receive token credits in exchange for a slice of their future sales, but neither Nvidia nor its partners has disclosed the revenue-split percentages.
  - e6 [fact] who: Sharon AI | Sharon AI disclosed on 2026-06-12 that its agreement runs for six years and covers 72 MW of new Australian data-center capacity, scaling to as many as 40,000 Grace Blackwell GB300 GPUs. | quote: In an 8-K filing dated June 12th, Sharon AI disclosed that the agreement runs for six years and covers 72 MW of new Australian data center capacity built to Nvidia's DSX AI factory design, scaling to as many as 40,000 Grace Blackwell GB300 
  - e7 [fact] who: Sharon AI | Sharon AI disclosed in its CY25 results a revenue-share facility of up to $200 million with Digital Alpha. | quote: The Nasdaq-listed neocloud separately holds a revenue-share facility of up to $200 million with investor Digital Alpha, disclosed in its CY25 results
  - e8 [rumour] who: Tom's Hardware | Firmus is building a DSX-aligned campus in Batam expected to scale to 360 MW and house up to 170,000 Nvidia GPUs. | quote: Firmus is building a DSX-aligned campus in Batam, Indonesia, that’s expected to scale to 360 MW and house up to 170,000 Nvidia GPUs.
  - e9 [third_party_view] who: Tom's Hardware | Tom's Hardware reported that Nvidia participated for $30 billion in OpenAI's $110 billion funding round and backed xAI's $20 billion Colossus 2 financing. | quote: Nvidia has spent much of the last year funnelling cash directly to its customers, including a $30 billion participation in OpenAI's $110 billion funding round and backing for xAI's $20 billion Colossus 2 financing
  - e10 [third_party_view] who: Tom's Hardware | Tom's Hardware characterized Nvidia as running roughly 75% gross margins; the passage gives no specific reporting period. | quote: a supplier already running roughly 75% gross margins

Return one placement per statement id, in order.

Why did you return no links for e6 about Sharon AI’s six-year agreement, 72 MW, and up to 40,000 GPUs? Which exact original instruction and source statements did you rely on? Which two alternative interpretations did you reject, and why? Separate what was shown from what you inferred.
